newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan investors to boost cash holdings in April.
newsitem.headline: Japan investors to boost cash holdings in April.

text.p: Japanese institutional investors plan to increase the weighting of cash holdings in their portfolios in April while reducing their bond and equity holdings, a Reuters investment survey showed on Friday.
Investors do not expect any major disruptions in the key markets in April, which are expected to move in a narrow range, the survey showed.

In the survey, the average overall weighting of cash holdings rose 2.67 percentage points from the previous survey to 15.00 percent. The average overall portfolio weighting of bonds fell to 39.42 percent percent, down 1.08 percentage point, and the average overall weighting of equities was 1.59 points lower at 45.58 percent.
The Reuters monthly Global Asset Allocation survey asked 16 Japan-based financial institutions in late March about their investment strategies for April.
Within the equities portfolio, the weighting of shares in German, French, Japanese and emerging markets rose while the weighting of U.S. and British shares fell.
Despite the increase in the weighting of Japanese equities, many domestic investors expect the Tokyo stock market to stay bearish in and after April.

They said the impact of a planned rise in the sales tax, prospects for Japan's "Big Bang" financial deregulation and the possible use of more tax money to solve bad loan problems were were all factors which may sway the Japanese stock market.
The possible sales of securities as a means for companies to unload bad assets and the selloff of stocks in companies that report poor earnings were also worrisome, they said.
Investors view European markets favourably as the current economic climate and corporate earnings in those countries were seen having a good impact on their stock markets.

On the U.S. market, their main interest was in first-quarter 1997 corporate earnings, which many expected to be positive. But some investors worried that some U.S. companies' growth may slow due to such factors as the strong dollar, slowing demand and rising wages.
The recent rise in the key U.S. interest rate is expected make it easier for investors to act by taking away the uncertainty factor from the market, they said.
But some still saw a need to closely watch market participants' reaction to upcoming U.S. economic data because of speculation that another rate rise is in the works.
In the Reuter bond portfolio survey, the weighting of U.S. and French markets fell but other European markets, particularly Germany, rose in favour.
Investors surveyed unanimously believe that Japan will continue its policy of very low interest rates.

They said they are not too worried about the impact of the rise in interest rates in the United States, and added that if there was another hike by the U.S. Federal Reserve, it would be to prevent an over-heating in its economy.
Weightings are generally higher in European markets as investors think there is a relatively small possibility of interest rate rises in Europe.
